class.name: PathSearch
class.brief_description: Weighted A* search over a graph of connections between nodes, for agents that walk between the points where they jump, climb or pass through something.
class.description: Searches a graph whose nodes are areas an agent can move freely within and whose connections are the points where it leaves one node for another: a jump, a climb, a door. The search runs over connections rather than nodes, so what a connection costs to reach depends on where the one before it landed, and the agent's own position prices the first connections out of the start node. The caller keeps the graph as packed arrays indexed by connection and node ids, built however it likes, and hands them over per call; only the search lives here, for speed. Packed arrays are copy-on-write, so a search keeps reading the arrays it was given even if the caller patches its own copies meanwhile, which makes [method find_path] safe to call from a worker thread.

method.name: find_path
method.description: Finds the cheapest known sequence of connections from [param start_node], where the actor stands at [param actor_position], to [param goal_node], heading for [param goal_position] within it. [param graph] holds the connection arrays, all of one size, one entry per connection id: [code]connection_position[/code] ([PackedVector2Array], where the actor has to get to), [code]connection_landing[/code] ([PackedVector2Array], where it ends up after taking it), [code]connection_runup_x[/code] ([PackedFloat32Array], the x of the runup point) and [code]connection_runup_sign[/code] ([PackedInt32Array], the sign of the direction the connection has to be approached in, or 0 for none), [code]connection_cost[/code] ([PackedFloat64Array], the connection's own cost), [code]connection_level[/code] ([PackedByteArray], the ability level it requires), [code]connection_flags[/code] ([PackedByteArray], [constant CONNECTION_FLAG_ACTIVE], [constant CONNECTION_FLAG_CLOSED] and [constant CONNECTION_FLAG_LOCKED]), [code]connection_key[/code] ([PackedInt32Array], the key that opens it while locked), [code]connection_start_node[/code] and [code]connection_end_node[/code] ([PackedInt32Array], its node ids). It also holds the node arrays, one entry per node id: [code]node_active[/code] ([PackedByteArray], non-zero for nodes that can be passed through), [code]node_is_climb[/code] ([PackedByteArray], non-zero where reaching a connection also means climbing to its height), and node N's outgoing connection ids as [code]node_connection_ids[/code] ([PackedInt32Array]) from index [code]node_connection_begin[N][/code] up to [code]node_connection_begin[N + 1][/code] ([PackedInt32Array], one entry longer than the node count). A connection is skipped unless it's active, leads into an active node and requires at most [param actor_level]. A closed and locked one is also skipped unless [param actor_key] is its key, and a key of [constant KEY_NONE] admits nobody. A connection leading straight back into the node the current one came from is never taken. [param costs] tunes the search: [code]walk_cost_per_unit[/code] (what a unit of horizontal distance walked between connections costs), [code]heuristic_per_unit[/code] (what a unit of straight-line distance still to the goal counts for; more than the walk cost trades path quality for fewer iterations), [code]climb_vertical_mult[/code] (on a climb node, how many walked units a unit of height to the connection counts as), [code]heuristic_up_mult[/code] and [code]heuristic_down_mult[/code] (how much a unit of height still to climb or drop to the goal counts in the heuristic). The search gives up after [param max_iterations] iterations. [param stop_at_step] makes it stop at that iteration and return the partial path to the connection it was about to expand, for stepping through a search; pass [constant NO_STOP] to run to the end. Returns a dictionary with [code]path[/code] (a [PackedInt32Array] of connection ids in travel order, empty if there is no path, the search gave up or the start and goal nodes are the same), [code]steps[/code] (the iterations taken) and [code]edges[/code] (the outgoing connections looked at, over all iterations).

constants.constant: Flag of a connection that can be taken at all. Connections without it are skipped outright.
Flag of a connection that is shut, like a closed door. Anyone may open it unless it's also locked.
Flag of a connection that, while closed, only an actor whose key matches the connection's may open.
The key that opens nothing: a locked connection holding it admits nobody.
Value of the stop step that lets a search run to its end.
